title: Sample Size, Test Two Proportions New
howtouse:
To compute sample size: specify both group proportions and power
To compute power: specify both group proportions and sample size
To compute detectable proportion difference: specify sample size, power, and group 2 proportion

TIP: Any field below accepts a comma-separated list of values (e.g. 0.1,0.2,0.3). When more than one field has multiple values, every combination is computed and returned as a table, so you do not need to re-run this dialog for each scenario.
ratio: Group 1 vs Group 2 Sample Size Ratio (comma-separated for multiple values)
siglevel: Significance Level (0-1; comma-separated for multiple values)
legends: Show Legends and if so, position of Legends (default is right)

help.title: Sample Size, Test Two Proportions
help.body:
This is an assessment of sample size for a two-sample test of proportions. It computes the sample size, power, or effect size (difference in proportions, rate ratio, odds ratio) when the user specifies the other two.

Sample Size: Specify the number of subjects in the study. Comma-separated lists are accepted.

Power: Specify the desired power of the study, i.e. the probability that the test will reject the null hypothesis if the alternative hypothesis was true. Comma-separated lists are accepted.

Group 1 Proportion: Specify the proportion in group 1. Comma-separated lists are accepted.

Group 2 Proportion: Specify the proportion in group 2. Comma-separated lists are accepted.

Group 1 vs Group 2 Sample Size Ratio: Specify the desired ratio of the sample sizes (group 1 N divided by group 2 N). A ratio of 1 means equal sample sizes. Comma-separated lists are accepted.

Significance Level: Specify the desired significance level (i.e. type I error) of the test. Comma-separated lists are accepted.

Alternative Hypothesis: Specify whether the test is two-sided or one-sided

Generate Power Curve Plot: When multiple values are supplied for more than one field, check this box to plot the results. Choose which computed quantity goes on the X-axis, and optionally one or more fields to group/color separate curves by.

Required R Packages: epiR, ggplot2
